The second experiment used high catalyst concentration (0.2 M), which amplified dimerization/deactivation effects. To further discriminate across the entire set, we need to probe a different kinetic dimension—specifically, reversibility and product inhibition—by adding initial product. This will test whether product binding influences the kinetics, which is relevant for many mechanisms (e.g., those with explicit product inhibition or reversible steps) and may help differentiate within the top group as well.

In contrast, mechanisms without product sensitivity (e.g., irreversible deactivation pathways) may be less affected.
